questions.question: Some of the talas invented by _________ include Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi and Navamukhi.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**M. Balamuralikrishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **M. Balamuralikrishna** was an Indian Carnatic vocalist, musician, multi-instrumentalist, playback singer, composer, and character actor.
 
• He was known for his deep knowledge of both the theoretical and practical aspects of Carnatic music.
 
• He invented new ragas as well as talas, including the ones mentioned: Trimukhi, Panchamukhi, Saptamukhi, and Navamukhi.
 
• His contributions to Carnatic music earned him several prestigious awards, including the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Carnatic Music**

 
 
• Carnatic music is a system of music commonly associated with the southern part of the Indian subcontinent, with its foundations in ancient Hindu traditions.
 
• It is one of the two main subgenres of Indian classical music that evolved from ancient Hindu traditions, the other subgenre being Hindustani music.
 
• The main emphasis in Carnatic music is on vocal music; most compositions are written to be sung, and even when played on instruments, they are meant to be performed in a singing style (known as gayaki).
 
 
 
• **Tala**
 
 
• Tala, literally meaning "clap," is the term used in Indian classical music to refer to musical meter, that is, any rhythmic beat or strike that measures musical time.
 
• It is a series of beats that are cyclically repeated.
 
• Talas can have different numbers of beats, and the cycle of beats is divided into sections called "angas," which can be of varying lengths.
 
 
 
• **Instruments Played by M. Balamuralikrishna**
 
 
• Besides being a renowned vocalist, M. Balamuralikrishna was proficient in playing the violin, viola, mridangam, and kanjira.
 
• His multifaceted talent in playing various instruments added to his versatility and depth as a musician.

questions.question: Lotia is a regional music form of which state?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rajasthan**__.

__
 
• **Lotia** is a **traditional folk music genre** originating from **Rajasthan, India**.
 
• It finds its cultural expression through the voices of peasants as they toil in the fields, particularly during the Lotia festival, which typically occurs in the Chaitra month of the Hindi calendar.
 
• Thematically, Lotia revolves around the significance of water. During the festival, women participate by carrying lotas (vessels used for fetching water) and kalash (vessels symbolizing auspiciousness in water-filling rituals) filled with water sourced from ponds and wells.
 
• These vessels are adorned with vibrant flowers before being brought home, adding to the festive ambiance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Rajasthan boasts a rich tapestry of regional folk music styles, each with its own unique characteristics and cultural significance:
 
 
• **Maand:** Regarded as one of the most refined forms of folk music in Rajasthan, Maand has its origins in the royal courts where it was performed to honor the Rajput monarchs. It narrates tales of valor and sacrifice associated with Rajasthan's warriors.
 
• Panihari: This genre of music revolves around the theme of water, featuring songs that often depict the unexpected encounters of lovers amidst its lyrical narratives.
 
• **Kurjaa, Pipli, Rattan Rano, Mumal, Ghughri, Kevda: **These are among the many folk songs originating from the Marwar region, each carrying its own distinctive melodies and stories reflective of the local culture and traditions.
 
• **Kamad, Bhopey, Langas, Mirasi, Kalawant: **These represent some of the prominent musician castes hailing from the Eastern Plain region of Rajasthan. Each caste brings forth its own musical traditions, contributing to the diverse and vibrant landscape of Rajasthani folk music.
